# How to write a simple system as one Rulpane link

Rulpane (<https://reny-develop.github.io/Rulpane/>) turns one link into a working screen: a
request and its approval, a checklist, a sign-off, a loan register, a booking, a roster. The
link carries everything — the rules, the layout, the look and where things stand — so there is
no server, no sign-up and nothing to install. Whoever opens the link uses the system, every
step rewrites the link, and sending the new link on hands over the system as it stands.

This page is everything needed to write one. It is meant to be read by a person or by an AI.

## If you are an AI asked to make a Rulpane link

1. Work out what can be done in the system, by whom, and when it is finished.
2. Write one **paneset** (below): a JSON document with the rules in `r`, the screen in `v`
   and, if it helps, where to start in `s`. Start from the complete example in
   [A whole paneset](#a-whole-paneset) and change it; do not invent keys or operations that
   are not on this page.
3. Give the person **the link**: `https://reny-develop.github.io/Rulpane/#p=` followed by the
   paneset as JSON on one line, with **every space written as `%20` — inside strings too, such
   as `"Mon%20am"`**, or a chat cuts the link at the first one. Nothing else needs encoding;
   other languages' characters may stay as they are.
4. Also give **the JSON itself** in a code block, and say: if the link does not open, paste
   the JSON into the editor at <https://reny-develop.github.io/Rulpane/#make>, press
   "Make link", and tell me the reason it shows. The reason names the key that is wrong.
5. Before answering, check the paneset against [Before you answer](#before-you-answer).
6. Say plainly what Rulpane cannot do (see [What a link cannot do](#what-a-link-cannot-do)),
   when the request needs it: anybody holding the link can take any step, and nothing is
   hidden from them.

## The link

```
https://reny-develop.github.io/Rulpane/#p=<paneset>
```

`<paneset>` is either the JSON of a paneset, on one line, or the name of one. The keys of a
paneset can also be given one by one, `#r=…&v=…&t=…&s=…&b=…`; each takes a name or a JSON
document the same way, and one given in the link goes over the paneset's own:
`#p=expense-claim&t=paper` is that paneset in another theme. A JSON value runs to its own end,
so any `&`, `#` or `=` inside its strings is fine. Write a literal `%` in a string as `%25`.

Once the link is opened, every step rewrites it into a shorter packed form (`z:` followed by
deflated base64url). That form is for the page; never write it by hand.

## A paneset

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "rulpane/paneset/v1",   // required
  "r": …,   // the rules: a rule set document, or the name of one — required
  "v": …,   // the view: what the screen shows, and where — optional
  "t": …,   // the theme: colours, corners, type, spacing — optional
  "s": …,   // where to start: the state's data — optional; the rules' own start without it
  "b": …    // which of the rules' names the view reads under other names — optional
}
```

The paneset, a view and a theme each **must** carry their `$schema` (`rulpane/paneset/v1`,
`rulealize/view/v1`, `rulealize/theme/v1`); one without it is refused. A rule set's `$schema`
is only a label. Each of `r`, `v` and `t` is the document written in place, or a name:

| Key | Names that exist |
| --- | --- |
| `r` | bundled: `approval`, `checklist`, `request`, `roster`, `signatures`; from the [Rulealize Registry](https://github.com/reny-develop/Rulealize.Registry) as `<id>@<x.y.z>`, such as `Rulealize.RuleSet.Request@1.1.0` |
| `v` | bundled: `approval`, `progress`, `roster`, `stages`; from the Gallery as `<owner>/<name>@<n>` |
| `t` | bundled: `meadow`, `paper`; from the Gallery as `<owner>/<name>@<n>` |
| `p` | bundled: `expense-claim`, `onboarding`, `shift-request`, `shift-roster`, `sign-off`; from the Gallery as `<owner>/<name>@<n>` |

A new system almost always writes `r` and `v` in place. `s` is the state's `data`: an object
with one value per field of the rules' `state.schema`. Give it when the people, items or
steps of this one instance are not in the rules (they usually should not be: see
[State](#state)).

## A whole paneset

A loan register for the office's laptops. It opens as it is: copy it and change it.

```json paneset
{
  "$schema": "rulpane/paneset/v1",
  "r": {
    "$schema": "rulealize/ruleset/v1",
    "id": "laptop-loans",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "requires": [
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.TypeSchema", "version": "^1.3" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.State", "version": "^1.0" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Sequence", "version": "^1.4" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Record", "version": "^1.0" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Comparison", "version": "^1.0" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Logic", "version": "^1.0" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Binding", "version": "^1.0" },
      { "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Definition", "version": "^1.0" }
    ],
    "state": {
      "schema": {
        "laptops": { "op": "type.list", "element": { "op": "type.string", "minLength": 1 } },
        "loans": {
          "op": "type.list",
          "element": {
            "op": "rec.of",
            "fields": {
              "laptop": { "op": "type.string", "minLength": 1 },
              "who": { "op": "type.string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 40 }
            }
          }
        }
      },
      "initial": { "laptops": ["lt-01", "lt-02", "lt-03"], "loans": [] }
    },
    "definitions": {
      "out": {
        "op": "seq.select", "source": "$loans", "as": "l",
        "select": { "op": "rec.at", "record": "@l", "key": "laptop" }
      },
      "available": {
        "op": "seq.where", "source": "$laptops", "as": "x",
        "predicate": {
          "op": "logic.not",
          "value": { "op": "seq.any", "source": "#out", "as": "o", "predicate": { "op": "cmp.eq", "left": "@o", "right": "@x" } }
        }
      }
    },
    "inputs": {
      "lend": {
        "params": {
          "laptop": { "domain": "#available" },
          "who": { "open": { "op": "type.string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 40 } }
        },
        "effects": [
          {
            "op": "state.set", "path": "loans",
            "value": { "op": "seq.concat", "of": ["$loans", { "op": "seq.of", "of": [{ "laptop": "@laptop", "who": "@who" }] }] }
          }
        ]
      },
      "giveBack": {
        "params": { "laptop": { "domain": "#out" } },
        "effects": [
          {
            "op": "state.set", "path": "loans",
            "value": {
              "op": "seq.where", "source": "$loans", "as": "l",
              "predicate": { "op": "cmp.ne", "left": { "op": "rec.at", "record": "@l", "key": "laptop" }, "right": "@laptop" }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "projections": {
      "available": "#available",
      "loans": "$loans",
      "counts": {
        "free": { "op": "seq.count", "source": "#available" },
        "out": { "op": "seq.count", "source": "$loans" }
      }
    }
  },
  "v": {
    "$schema": "rulealize/view/v1",
    "title": "Laptop loans",
    "layout": [
      { "c": "stats", "items": [ { "label": "Free", "bind": "counts.free" }, { "label": "On loan", "bind": "counts.out" } ] },
      { "c": "table", "title": "On loan", "bind": "loans", "columns": [ { "key": "laptop", "label": "Laptop" }, { "key": "who", "label": "Borrower" } ] },
      { "c": "actions", "title": "Lend one", "inputs": ["lend"], "as": "select" },
      { "c": "actions", "title": "Take one back", "inputs": ["giveBack"] },
      { "c": "list", "title": "Free now", "bind": "available" }
    ],
    "names": {
      "inputs": { "lend": "Lend", "giveBack": "Take back" },
      "params": { "laptop": "Laptop", "who": "Borrower" }
    }
  }
}
```

A short one as a link, naming bundled parts (spaces would be `%20`; this one has none):

```text link
https://reny-develop.github.io/Rulpane/#p={"$schema":"rulpane/paneset/v1","r":"approval","v":"approval","t":"paper"}
```

## Rules

The rules are a [Rulealize](https://github.com/reny-develop/Rulealize) rule set: a JSON
document that says what a position looks like, what may be done to one, and when there is
nothing left to do. The screen asks it three things — what can be done now, where a step
leads, and whether it is over — and computes nothing itself.

### The top-level keys

These and no others; a misspelt key is refused, not ignored.

| Key | What it is | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$schema` | `"rulealize/ruleset/v1"` | optional label |
| `id`, `version` | a name, and a version `x.y.z` | required |
| `requires` | every plugin the document uses, as `{ "plugin": "<id>", "version": "^<x.y>" }` | required in practice |
| `state` | `schema` (the fields and their types) and `initial` (one value per field) | required |
| `inputs` | the named things that may be done | required |
| `definitions` | expressions given a name, written once and used as `#name` | optional |
| `projections` | named values the screen shows, computed from the state | optional |
| `terminal` | `when` it is over, and the `result` to call the ending | optional |
| `uses`, `held` | rule sets this one is made of | optional, rarely needed |

### Nodes and shorthands

Everything below those keys is a value or a **node**: an object with an `op`, such as
`{ "op": "cmp.eq", "left": "$stage", "right": "draft" }`. The part of `op` before the dot names
the plugin it comes from, and that plugin must be in `requires`. Wherever a value goes, a node
may go instead. An object without an `op` is a record whose values are evaluated, so
`{ "laptop": "@laptop", "who": "@who" }` builds a record. A JSON array is **not** a list where an
expression goes: write `{ "op": "seq.of", "of": [ … ] }`.

| Written | Means | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"$total"` | the state field `total` | `Rulealize.Plugin.State` |
| `"@n"` | the parameter `n`, or a name bound by `as` | `Rulealize.Plugin.Binding` |
| `"#open"` | the definition `open` | `Rulealize.Plugin.Definition` |

Text that has to start with `$`, `@` or `#` is written `{ "op": "literal", "value": "#1" }`.

Every operation is one of four kinds, and the kind decides where it may be written:

| Kind | Does | Goes in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| expression | computes a value | `when`, `domain`, effect values, `projections`, `terminal`, `definitions` |
| effect | writes to the state | only in an input's `effects` |
| schema | declares a type | `state.schema`, and a parameter's `open` |
| draw | picks at random, in the browser | only inside `effects` |

### State

```jsonc
"state": {
  "schema":  { "stage": { "op": "type.enum", "values": ["draft", "review", "done"] } },
  "initial": { "stage": "draft" }
}
```

Every field has a type, from a schema operation (`type.*`, `rec.of`, `rec.map`, …). Ask of each
field whether it is a rule or this instance: the people, items, steps and amounts of one case
belong in the state (`initial`, or the paneset's `s`), so that one rule set serves every case.
Lists of them are `type.list` with an `element` type, and a list of records is `type.list` of
`rec.of`.

### Inputs

```jsonc
"inputs": {
  "reject": {
    "params":   { "reason": { "domain": { "op": "seq.of", "of": ["scope", "cost"] } } },
    "actor":    "reviewer",
    "when":     { "op": "cmp.eq", "left": "$stage", "right": "review" },
    "validate": [ { "require": <expression:Boolean>, "code": "reason.missing" } ],
    "effects":  [ { "op": "state.set", "path": "stage", "value": "rejected" },
                  { "op": "state.set", "path": "reason", "value": "@reason" } ]
  }
}
```

- `effects` (required) — what it does, in order. An input's name may not contain `.`.
- `params` — each parameter has exactly one of:
  - `domain`: an expression giving the list of values it may take. Each value is a separate
    step on the screen, a button or an entry in a list to pick from.
  - `open`: a schema node, for a value somebody types — a name, an amount, a date as text. The
    screen shows a form field, held to the schema. `{ "field": "name" }` takes the schema of the
    state field `name`. An open parameter may be read in `effects` and `validate`, never in
    `when`, `actor` or a domain.
- `when` — whether the input is allowed now. Left out, it always is.
- `validate` — checked when an open value arrives; each clause's `code` is the refusal shown
  under the field when `require` is false. **Every clause must read an open parameter**; a
  condition on the state or on a `domain` parameter alone is refused here and belongs in `when`
  (which may read domain parameters, so "only a free slot" is `when`, not `validate`).
- `actor` — a label for whose step this is. The screen groups steps by it. **Nobody signs in:**
  anybody holding the link can take any step; the label only says whose it is meant to be.

### Definitions, projections and the end

```jsonc
"definitions": {
  "open":  { "op": "seq.where", "source": "$steps", "as": "s", "predicate": … },
  "owner": { "params": ["id"], "body": { "op": "rec.at", "record": "$owners", "key": "@id" } }
},
"projections": { "summary": { "stage": "$stage", "left": { "op": "seq.count", "source": "#open" } } },
"terminal":    { "when": { "op": "cmp.eq", "left": "$stage", "right": "done" }, "result": "$stage" }
```

A definition is read as `#name`; one with `params` is called with
`{ "op": "def.call", "def": "owner", "args": { "id": "@who" } }`. Definitions may not call
themselves. Projections are what a view binds to, and any shape: a value, a list, a record.
When `terminal.when` is true the screen shows the `result` and offers nothing more — though
steps whose `when` still holds are still listed by the rules, so write `when` to stop them.

### Values and null

Values are null, booleans, numbers (no integer/fraction split), text, lists, records and a
plugin's own values (a grid coordinate). Values of different kinds are never equal: `1` is not
`"1"`. A lookup that finds nothing gives `null` — past the end of a list, a missing key, off a
board — and `null` equals only `null`; ordering or arithmetic on `null` is an error. Rules lean
on that: no bounds check is needed before `rec.at` or `seq.elementAt`.

### requires

List every plugin whose operations the document uses, including State for `$`, Binding for `@`
and Definition for `#`. These are the versions Rulpane runs:

| Plugin | Write |
| --- | --- |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Arithmetic` (`math.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Arithmetic", "version": "^1.1" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Binding` (`bind.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Binding", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Branch` (`branch.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Branch", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Chance` (`chance.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Chance", "version": "^1.1" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Comparison` (`cmp.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Comparison", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Deck` (`deck.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Deck", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Definition` (`def.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Definition", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Graph` (`graph.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Graph", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Grid` (`grid.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Grid", "version": "^1.2" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Logic` (`logic.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Logic", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Record` (`rec.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Record", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Secret` (`secret.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Secret", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Sequence` (`seq.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Sequence", "version": "^1.4" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.State` (`state.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.State", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Text` (`str.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Text", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.Tuple` (`tuple.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.Tuple", "version": "^1.0" }` |
| `Rulealize.Plugin.TypeSchema` (`type.`) | `{ "plugin": "Rulealize.Plugin.TypeSchema", "version": "^1.3" }` |

### Operations

Every operation Rulpane can run. `<expr>` is any expression; `<expr:Number>` one giving a
number; `<schema>` a schema node; `<state field>` a field written `"$name"`.

Kind: `Expr` expression, `Effect`, `Schema`, `Draw` (an expression allowed only inside an input's `effects`). `"k"?:` marks an optional key.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Arithmetic (`math`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `math.add` | Expr | `{"op":"math.add","of":[<expr:Number>…]}` | sum; empty → 0 |
| `math.mul` | Expr | `{"op":"math.mul","of":[<expr:Number>…]}` | product; empty → 1 |
| `math.sub` | Expr | `{"op":"math.sub","left":<expr:Number>,"right":<expr:Number>}` | left − right |
| `math.div` | Expr | `{"op":"math.div","left":<expr:Number>,"right":<expr:Number>}` | not integer division (7/2 = 3.5); right 0 → fault |
| `math.mod` | Expr | `{"op":"math.mod","left":<expr:Number>,"right":<expr:Number>}` | remainder, sign of left (−7 mod 3 = −1); right 0 → fault |
| `math.min` | Expr | `{"op":"math.min","of":[<expr:Number>…]}` | smallest; empty → fault |
| `math.max` | Expr | `{"op":"math.max","of":[<expr:Number>…]}` | largest; empty → fault |
| `math.abs` | Expr | `{"op":"math.abs","value":<expr:Number>}` | absolute value |
| `math.round` | Expr | `{"op":"math.round","value":<expr:Number>,"scale"?:<int 0–28>,"mode":"halfAwayFromZero"\|"halfEven"\|"towardZero"\|"floor"\|"ceiling"}` | to `scale` places (default 0); `mode` required |

Any non-Number operand, `null` included, → fault: flatten with `cmp.coalesce` first.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Binding (`bind`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bind.let` | Expr | `{"op":"bind.let","bind":{"<name>":<expr>…},"in":<expr>}` | binds in written order (later reads earlier), returns `in` |
| `bind.local` | Expr | `{"op":"bind.local","name":"<name>"}`, sugar `"@<name>"` | a `bind.let` name, an `as`, or a param; unbound → build error |

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Branch (`branch`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branch.if` | Expr | `{"op":"branch.if","cond":<expr:Boolean>,"then":<expr>,"else"?:<expr>}` | untaken branch not evaluated; false, no `else` → null; non-Bool `cond` → fault |
| `branch.match` | Expr | `{"op":"branch.match","value":<expr>,"cases":{"<key>":<expr>…},"default"?:<expr>}` | exact match on canonical text (`true`→"true", `1.0`→"1", null→"null"); no match, no `default` → fault |

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Chance (`chance`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chance.pick` | Draw | `{"op":"chance.pick","of":<expr:Sequence>,"as"?:"<name>","weight"?:<expr:Number>}` | one element; `weight` reads it as `@<name>`, relative, 0 drops it; none → equal; nothing left or negative → fault |
| `chance.roll` | Draw | `{"op":"chance.roll","faces":<expr:Number>}` | 1…faces, equally likely; < 1 → fault |

A draw is allowed only inside `inputs.*.effects` (any depth). Every evaluation draws anew and effects read the snapshot, so use the drawn value in the one effect that draws it.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Comparison (`cmp`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cmp.eq` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.eq","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | null-safe; kinds differ → false (1 ≠ "1") |
| `cmp.ne` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.ne","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | not `cmp.eq` |
| `cmp.lt` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.lt","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | left < right |
| `cmp.lte` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.lte","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | left ≤ right |
| `cmp.gt` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.gt","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | left > right |
| `cmp.gte` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.gte","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | left ≥ right |
| `cmp.compare` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.compare","left":<expr>,"right":<expr>}` | `"lt"`/`"eq"`/`"gt"` |
| `cmp.isNull` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.isNull","value":<expr>}` | is null |
| `cmp.coalesce` | Expr | `{"op":"cmp.coalesce","of":[<expr>…]}` | first non-null; none → null |

Ordering and `compare`: Number, Text (ordinal), Bool only; null or mixed kinds → fault.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Deck (`deck`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deck.of` | Schema | `{"op":"deck.of","cards":["<card>"…]}` | pile; JSON counts, zeros omitted: `{"A":4}`, `{}` |
| `deck.count` | Expr | `{"op":"deck.count","of":<expr:pile>,"card":<expr:Text>}` | copies of a card; none → 0 |
| `deck.size` | Expr | `{"op":"deck.size","of":<expr:pile>}` | total cards |
| `deck.cards` | Expr | `{"op":"deck.cards","of":<expr:pile>}` | cards held, declared order (a domain) |
| `deck.draw` | Draw | `{"op":"deck.draw","of":<expr:pile>}` | a card weighted by count; empty → fault |
| `deck.move` | Effect | `{"op":"deck.move","from":<state field>,"to":<state field>,"card":<expr:Text>,"count"?:<expr:Number>}` | moves `count` (default 1); too few → fault |

`from`/`to` are `deck.of` fields (`"$deck"`). Dealing: `deck.draw` as `deck.move`'s `card`.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Definition (`def`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `def.ref` | Expr | `{"op":"def.ref","name":"<name>"}`, sugar `"#<name>"` | a definition with no `params` |
| `def.call` | Expr | `{"op":"def.call","def":"<name>","args":{"<param>":<expr>…}}` | `args` keys = `params` exactly |

`"definitions":{"<name>":{"params"?:["<name>"…],"body":<expr>}}`; no `body` key → the entry is the body (`"max":2`). A body sees `$`, `#` and its params only. Any cycle → build error.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Graph (`graph`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `graph.of` | Schema | `{"op":"graph.of","nodes":["<node>"…],"edges"?:{"<node>":["<node>"…]},"directed"?:bool,"value":<schema>}` | fixed graph; JSON one key per node |
| `graph.at` | Expr | `{"op":"graph.at","graph":<state field>,"node":<expr:Text>}` | value at node; null/unknown → null |
| `graph.adjacent` | Expr | `{"op":"graph.adjacent","graph":<state field>,"node":<expr:Text>,"direction"?:"out"\|"in"\|"either"}` | neighbours, `nodes` order; null/unknown → null |
| `graph.reachable` | Expr | `{"op":"graph.reachable","graph":<state field>,"from":<expr:Text>,"direction"?:"out"\|"in"\|"either","as"?:"<name>","through"?:<expr:Boolean>}` | BFS incl. `from`; `through` gates entering `@<name>`; null/unknown → null |
| `graph.set` | Effect | `{"op":"graph.set","target":<state field>,"node":<expr:Text>,"value":<expr>}` | write; null/unknown node → fault |

`graph`/`target` must be a `graph.of` field (`"$rooms"`). `direction` (default `"out"`) on an undirected graph, or `as` without `through` → build error.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Grid (`grid`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grid.board` | Schema | `{"op":"grid.board","width":<int>,"height":<int>,"coord"?:"index"\|"algebraic","cell":<schema>}` | board; JSON sparse, nulls omitted: `{"d4":"white"}` |
| `grid.square` | Schema | `{"op":"grid.square","width":<int>,"height":<int>,"coord"?:"index"\|"algebraic","nullable"?:bool}` | one coordinate; JSON `"e3"` |
| `grid.at` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.at","grid":<expr:board>,"coord":<expr:coord>}` | square; empty/off board/null → null |
| `grid.coords` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.coords","of":<expr:board>}` | all coords, row-major from top left |
| `grid.cells` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.cells","of":<expr:board>}` | all values, same order |
| `grid.ray` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.ray","grid":<expr:board>,"from":<expr:coord>,"dir":<expr:direction>,"length"?:<expr:Number>}` | coords to the edge, `from` excluded; bad `from` → empty |
| `grid.directions` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.directions","of":<expr:board>,"kind":"orthogonal"\|"diagonal"\|"eight"\|"axis"}` | 4/4/8; `axis`: 1,0 0,1 1,1 1,-1 |
| `grid.run` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.run","grid":<expr:board>,"from":<expr:coord>,"axis":<expr:direction>,"value":<expr>}` | line of `value` through `from`, both ways, `from` counts 1 unread; bad `from` → 0 |
| `grid.with` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.with","grid":<expr:board>,"coord":<expr:coord>,"value":<expr>}` | new board, one square set |
| `grid.withMany` | Expr | `{"op":"grid.withMany","grid":<expr:board>,"coords":<expr:Sequence>,"value":<expr>}` | new board, squares set |
| `grid.set` | Effect | `{"op":"grid.set","target":<state field>,"coord":<expr:coord>,"value":<expr>}` | write one square |
| `grid.setMany` | Effect | `{"op":"grid.setMany","target":<state field>,"coords":<expr:Sequence>,"value":<expr>}` | `value` (once) to each |

Coords are text: `algebraic` `"a1"` bottom-left, y up (width ≤ 26); `index` `"x,y"`, `"0,0"` top-left, y down. Directions are `"dx,dy"` (`"0,-1"`). `target` is a `grid.board` field (`"$board"`). Off-board/null coord: reads → null, `with`/`set` forms → fault. Empty squares need `cell` `"nullable":true`. Store a coord in `grid.square`, not `type.string` (Text ≠ coord).

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Logic (`logic`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `logic.and` | Expr | `{"op":"logic.and","all":[<expr:Boolean>…]}` | in order, stops at false; empty → true |
| `logic.or` | Expr | `{"op":"logic.or","any":[<expr:Boolean>…]}` | in order, stops at true; empty → false |
| `logic.not` | Expr | `{"op":"logic.not","value":<expr:Boolean>}` | negation |
| `logic.xor` | Expr | `{"op":"logic.xor","of":[<expr:Boolean>…]}` | odd count true; all evaluated |

Non-Bool (null too) → fault.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Record (`rec`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rec.of` | Schema | `{"op":"rec.of","fields":{"<key>":<schema>…}}` | named fields |
| `rec.map` | Schema | `{"op":"rec.map","keys":["<key>"…],"value":<schema>}` | declared keys, one value schema |
| `rec.at` | Expr | `{"op":"rec.at","record":<expr>,"key":<expr:Text>}` | absent key → fault; null record → null |
| `rec.has` | Expr | `{"op":"rec.has","record":<expr>,"key":<expr:Text>}` | key exists |
| `rec.with` | Expr | `{"op":"rec.with","record":<expr>,"key":<expr>,"value":<expr>}` | copy, key replaced; new key → fault |
| `rec.keys` | Expr | `{"op":"rec.keys","of":<expr>}` | keys, ordinal order |
| `rec.set` | Effect | `{"op":"rec.set","target":<state field>,"key":<expr>,"value":<expr>}` | write key; new key → fault |
| `rec.update` | Effect | `{"op":"rec.update","target":<state field>,"key":<expr>,"as":"<name>","value":<expr>}` | `@<name>` = whole record; result written at `key` |

`target` is a `rec.of`/`rec.map` field (`"$hand"`); `"hand.black"` is not a path. A record value is an object without `op`: `{"a":"@x"}`. Records cannot be input arguments.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Secret (`secret`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secret.of` | Schema | `{"op":"secret.of","owners":["<owner>"…],"value":<schema>}` | JSON keyed by owner, unsealed omitted |
| `secret.sealed` | Expr | `{"op":"secret.sealed","of":<expr:sealed>,"owner":<expr:Text>}` | owner has sealed |
| `secret.all` | Expr | `{"op":"secret.all","of":<expr:sealed>}` | all have sealed |
| `secret.waiting` | Expr | `{"op":"secret.waiting","of":<expr:sealed>}` | owners yet to seal (a domain) |
| `secret.open` | Expr | `{"op":"secret.open","of":<expr:sealed>,"owner":<expr:Text>}` | sealed value; unsealed → null |
| `secret.seal` | Effect | `{"op":"secret.seal","target":<state field>,"owner":<expr:Text>,"value":<expr>}` | resealing, null, unknown owner → fault |
| `secret.clear` | Effect | `{"op":"secret.clear","target":<state field>,"owner"?:<expr:Text>}` | discards all, or one owner's |

`of`/`target` is a `secret.of` field (`"$hands"`). Rules may read a seal; it tells the host what to hide. To reveal, copy via `secret.open` into a field in the input that clears.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Sequence (`seq`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seq.empty` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.empty"}` | empty sequence |
| `seq.of` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.of","of":[<expr>…]}` | the listed elements |
| `seq.range` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.range","from":<expr:Number>,"count":<expr:Number>}` | `count` integers from `from`; negative → fault |
| `seq.any` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.any","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as"?:"<name>","predicate"?:<expr:Boolean>}` | some `@<name>` passes; no predicate → non-empty |
| `seq.count` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.count","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as"?:"<name>","where"?:<expr:Boolean>}` | count passing `@<name>`; no `where` → length |
| `seq.sum` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.sum","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as"?:"<name>","select"?:<expr:Number>}` | total of `select` per `@<name>` or of elements; empty → 0 |
| `seq.elementAt` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.elementAt","source":<expr:Sequence>,"index":<expr:Number>}` | 0-based; past the end → null; negative → fault |
| `seq.takeWhile` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.takeWhile","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as":"<name>","predicate":<expr:Boolean>}` | elements before first failing `@<name>` |
| `seq.where` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.where","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as":"<name>","predicate":<expr:Boolean>}` | those passing `@<name>` |
| `seq.select` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.select","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as":"<name>","select":<expr>}` | each `@<name>` projected |
| `seq.selectMany` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.selectMany","source":<expr:Sequence>,"as":"<name>","select":<expr:Sequence>}` | concat of `select` per `@<name>` |
| `seq.concat` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.concat","of":[<expr:Sequence>…]}` | joined in order |
| `seq.take` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.take","source":<expr:Sequence>,"count":<expr:Number>}` | first `count`; negative → fault |
| `seq.skip` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.skip","source":<expr:Sequence>,"count":<expr:Number>}` | all after `count`; negative → fault |
| `seq.replaceAt` | Expr | `{"op":"seq.replaceAt","source":<expr:Sequence>,"index":<expr:Number>,"as"?:"<name>","value":<expr>}` | `@<name>` = old element; out of range → unchanged; negative → fault |

`as` may be omitted only if the element is not read. `[1,2]` as an expression is not a sequence: use `seq.of`.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.State (`state`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state.get` | Expr | `{"op":"state.get","path":"<field>"}`, sugar `"$<field>"` | field value before any effect ran |
| `state.set` | Effect | `{"op":"state.set","path":"<field>","value":<expr>}` | write; last wins |
| `state.update` | Effect | `{"op":"state.update","path":"<field>","as":"<name>","value":<expr>}` | `@<name>` = current value |

`path` is a static top-level field name, never dotted.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Text (`str`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `str.trim` | Expr | `{"op":"str.trim","value":<expr:Text>}` | strip tab/LF/CR/space/U+3000 at ends |
| `str.length` | Expr | `{"op":"str.length","value":<expr:Text>}` | UTF-16 units |
| `str.contains` | Expr | `{"op":"str.contains","value":<expr:Text>,"part":<expr:Text>}` | holds `part`, case-sensitive |
| `str.startsWith` | Expr | `{"op":"str.startsWith","value":<expr:Text>,"part":<expr:Text>}` | starts with `part` |
| `str.endsWith` | Expr | `{"op":"str.endsWith","value":<expr:Text>,"part":<expr:Text>}` | ends with `part` |
| `str.slice` | Expr | `{"op":"str.slice","value":<expr:Text>,"from":<expr:Number>,"count"?:<expr:Number>}` | substring; past end cut short; negative → fault |
| `str.only` | Expr | `{"op":"str.only","value":<expr:Text>,"of":["<class>"…]}` | all units in the classes; `""` → true |

Classes: `asciiDigit` `asciiUpper` `asciiLower` `asciiLetter` `space` `hyphen` `hiragana` `katakana`. Non-Text (null too) → fault. Text starting `$ @ #` is shorthand: write `{"op":"literal","value":"@"}`.

#### Rulealize.Plugin.Tuple (`tuple`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tuple.of` | Expr | `{"op":"tuple.of","of":[<expr>…]}` | packed; text `"e2\|e4\|-"` |
| `tuple.at` | Expr | `{"op":"tuple.at","tuple":<expr>,"index":<int>}` | out of range → fault; null tuple → null |

For a compound input parameter. A null element leaves no canonical text: use a sentinel (`"-"`).

#### Rulealize.Plugin.TypeSchema (`type`)

| Op | Kind | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type.bool` | Schema | `{"op":"type.bool","nullable"?:bool}` | Bool |
| `type.int` | Schema | `{"op":"type.int","min"?:<int>,"max"?:<int>,"nullable"?:bool}` | whole number, inclusive |
| `type.decimal` | Schema | `{"op":"type.decimal","scale"?:<int 0–28>,"min"?:<number>,"max"?:<number>,"nullable"?:bool}` | ≤ `scale` places, never rounded |
| `type.string` | Schema | `{"op":"type.string","minLength"?:<int>,"maxLength"?:<int>,"nullable"?:bool}` | Text |
| `type.enum` | Schema | `{"op":"type.enum","values":["<value>"…],"nullable"?:bool}` | one of `values` |
| `type.list` | Schema | `{"op":"type.list","element":<schema>,"minLength"?:<int>,"maxLength"?:<int>}` | Sequence; JSON array |

Schema keys are static; `nullable` defaults to false.

## The view

Without `v`, the screen is made from the rules: their projections (or the state), every step
as a button grouped by actor and input, a form for open parameters, and the result at the end.
A view lays it out instead.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "rulealize/view/v1",
  "title": "Expense claim",
  "layout": [ /* blocks, top to bottom */ ],
  "names": { "inputs": { … }, "params": { … }, "codes": { … }, "values": { … } }
}
```

A **binding** (`bind`) is a projection name followed by `.`-separated steps into it
(`summary.stage`), or a state field as the rules write one (`$total`); a number steps into a
list. A path that leads nowhere shows `—`; a first name the rules do not have is refused.

| Block | Keys | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `heading` | `text` | a heading |
| `text` | `text` | a paragraph |
| `fields` | `title`?, `rows`: [{ `label`, `bind`, `tone`?, `showWhen`? }] | a card of label–value rows. `tone` maps a value to `neutral`, `accent`, `ok`, `warn` or `danger`, shown as a coloured chip |
| `stats` | `items`: [{ `label`, `bind` }] | values set large, side by side |
| `list` | `title`?, `bind` | a list's values side by side |
| `table` | `title`?, `bind`, `columns`?: [`key` or { `key`, `label` }] | a list of records, one per row; every key without `columns` |
| `board` | `title`?, `bind`, `play`?, `pieces`? | a Grid board in a state field (`$board`); `play` is `"input.param"` to make squares buttons; `pieces` maps values to `dark`, `light`, `accent`, `ok`, `warn`, `danger` |
| `actions` | `title`?, `inputs`, `as`? | the steps of the listed inputs, or `"*"` for every step; `"as": "select"` shows an input's choices as one list and a button. A block with nothing to offer now is hidden |

Every block, and every `fields` row, takes `showWhen`: a binding that must read `true` for it
to show. The view holds no conditions of its own; a projection says when.

`names` says what the screen calls the rules' own names, in the one language the view is
written in: `inputs` (step buttons), `params` (argument and field names), `codes` (refusals),
`values` (any value shown). A name left out is shown as the rules spell it. `title` replaces the
rule set's id in the heading.

A view meant for many rule sets declares `expects` — the projections it reads, with types, and
the inputs it names — and binds nothing else; the bundled `stages` and `progress` are such views.
`b` in the paneset then says where rules that call those things something else keep them:
`"b": { "all": "$steps", "done": "$done", "place": "game.place" }`.

## The theme

```json
{
  "$schema": "rulealize/theme/v1",
  "colors": { "light": { "accent": "#1f7a4d", "accent-soft": "#e4f4ea" }, "dark": { "accent": "#6fd6a0" } },
  "radius": "round",
  "font": "rounded",
  "density": "compact"
}
```

`colors.light` and `colors.dark` take any of `bg`, `surface`, `sunken`, `text`, `muted`, `line`,
`line-strong`, `accent`, `accent-hover`, `accent-text`, `accent-soft`, `mark`, `mark-text`, `ok`,
`ok-soft`, `danger`, `danger-soft`, `warn`, `warn-soft`, as `#rrggbb`. `radius` is `sharp`,
`default` or `round`; `font` is `inter`, `system`, `serif` or `rounded`; `density` is
`comfortable` or `compact`. Every pair of colours text is set in must reach a contrast of 4.5:1,
or the theme is refused with the pair that failed. The top bar keeps Rulpane's own look.

## What a link cannot do

- **Keep anything secret, or know who is who.** The whole state is in the link, and nobody signs
  in: anybody with the link sees everything and can take any step. Fine for a team's own
  hand-overs; not for votes, payments or anything to hide.
- **Be in two places at once.** Each step makes a new link. Two people working from the same
  link make two separate histories; send the link on, one person at a time.
- **Run code, load anything from elsewhere, or ask for passwords.** A link holds documents, not
  HTML or script; text in a view is shown as text. The top bar always says who made the screen.
- **Use plugins other than those above**, or more than a bounded amount of work per step.

## Before you answer

- [ ] The paneset, and `v` and `t` when written in place, each have their `$schema`.
- [ ] Every `op` is in [Operations](#operations), with only the keys its form shows.
- [ ] Every plugin whose `op`, `$`, `@` or `#` is used is in `requires`.
- [ ] Lists where an expression goes are `seq.of`, not JSON arrays (arrays are fine in
      `state.initial`, `s` and a view).
- [ ] No open parameter is read in `when`, `actor` or a `domain`; every `validate` clause reads one.
- [ ] Every view binding names a projection the rules have (or a state field as `$name`).
- [ ] The link is one line, and every space in it is `%20`.

## When it does not open

The page shows why, with the path to the node at fault, for instance:

```
/inputs/go/effects[0]/value: 'math.add' comes from Rulealize.Plugin.Arithmetic, which this rule set does not name in 'requires'.
/inputs/go/effects[0]/value: an array is not an expression. Sequences are produced by operations, never written down.
/state/schema: must declare at least one field.
```

The usual causes:

- an operation that is not in [Operations](#operations), or a key that is not in its form;
- a plugin used but missing from `requires`;
- a list written as a JSON array where an expression goes, instead of `seq.of`;
- an open parameter read in `when` or a domain, or a `validate` clause that reads none;
- a paneset, view or theme without its `$schema`;
- a view binding a projection the rules do not have, or a key a table's records do not have;
- the link cut at a space: write spaces as `%20`.
